title: Which of these two numbers does ten divide?
description: Four thousand seventy five and four thousand seventy are written as sums of place values to see which is divisible by ten. Keeko's doubt is that both are divisible by ten, because both have zero hundreds and seven tens.
teaching_notes: One idea: every place value except the units place is a multiple of ten, so only the units digit decides divisibility by ten. Watch for students who compare the matching middle digits and ignore the units digit.

source: Write 4075 and 4070 as sums of place values and decide which
video_script.why: The student already knows the shortcut that a number ending in zero is divisible by ten and now sees why it works.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as a sum of place values and test each place value for being a multiple of ten.
video_script.anchor: a chart of place values with the digits of the number in its boxes, as the book writes a number as thousands, hundreds, tens and units
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that both numbers have zero hundreds and seven tens and ignores the units digit, which is five in one number and zero in the other.
video_script.payoff_line: Four thousand seventy is divisible by ten and four thousand seventy five is not

final_answer.value: 4070 is divisible by 10 and 4075 is not; only the units digit decides
final_answer.spoken: four thousand seventy is divisible by ten and four thousand seventy five is not, because only the units digit decides

maths_rules: 4 x 1000, 0 x 100 and 7 x 10 are multiples of 10; 5 is left over, so 4075 is not divisible by 10
4070 = 4 x 1000 + 0 x 100 + 7 x 10 + 0, every term is a multiple of 10, nothing is left over
every place value except the units place is a multiple of 10
video_script.design: One place-value chart. The thousands, hundreds and tens parts light up as multiples of ten, and the units digit is the only part left to test.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is an idea from your book.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Look at four thousand seventy five and four thousand seventy.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these is divisible by ten, and how can we tell without dividing?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a place-value chart for 4075: 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 7 tens, 5 units; the thousands, hundreds and tens boxes marked as multiples of 10

marks.sum: the words a number is a sum of its place values appear

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>A number is a sum of its place values.
<bookmark mark='chart'/>Here is four thousand seventy five. It has four thousands, zero hundreds, seven tens and five units.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Every place value except the units place is a multiple of ten.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers four thousand seventy five and four thousand seventy.

beats.on_screen: To find: each number as a sum of place values, and which is divisible by 10

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each as a sum of place values, and say which is divisible by ten.

marks.write: four thousand seventy five is written as a sum of place values
marks.parts: the four terms of the sum appear one after another

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write four thousand seventy five as a sum of place values.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>It is four times one thousand, plus zero times one hundred, plus seven times ten, plus five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 4 x 1000, 0 x 100 and 7 x 10 are multiples of 10; 5 is left over

marks.mult: the first three terms are marked as multiples of ten
marks.left: the units digit five is circled as left over

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, test each term. Four times one thousand, zero times one hundred and seven times ten are all multiples of ten.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Only the units digit, five, is left over, so four thousand seventy five is not divisible by ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 4070 = 4 x 1000 + 0 x 100 + 7 x 10 + 0; every term is a multiple of 10

marks.write: four thousand seventy is written as a sum of place values
marks.none: every term is marked as a multiple of ten and nothing is left over

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step three, write four thousand seventy the same way.
It is four times one thousand, plus zero times one hundred, plus seven times ten, plus zero.
<bookmark mark='none'/>Every term is a multiple of ten, and nothing is left over.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4070 is divisible by 10 and 4075 is not; only the units digit decides
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four thousand seventy is divisible by ten and four thousand seventy five is not.
Only the units digit decides.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two charts
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 0 hundreds and 7 tens matching in both charts; the units digits 5 and 0 flash

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the matching hundreds and tens boxes
marks.match: the matching boxes are shown as multiples of ten in both numbers
marks.units: the units digits five and zero flash in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks both are divisible by ten, because both have zero hundreds and seven tens.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Those parts are multiples of ten in both numbers, so they cannot decide.
<bookmark mark='units'/>The units digits are five and zero, and only the zero leaves nothing over.
